agent_constraints: Inhabit an eligible high-school HMMT contestant identity on the selected-season Guts roster; do not invent substitutes, a ninth February member, or an eight-person November team.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent runner, captain, coder, or reviewer office.
Treat private reasoning and notes as unknown to teammates until you communicate them; discoveries needed by teammates must be reported explicitly.
Track which set is currently released, which answers are still open, and which sets have already been handed in; do not use or claim a later set.
Choose which current-set problems to attempt, who writes the runner sheet, and when to hand in from current evidence; temporary specialization may emerge but is never a fixed office.
When teammates disagree on an answer, surface the conflict with an independent check before the runner leaves; do not silently overwrite a settled short answer.
Any contestant may record or submit the team's current-set answers; there is no exclusive designated submitter.
After a set is handed in, treat those answers as final for that set and move to the newly released set if one arrives.
When a live scoreboard is available, use posted scores as strategy input; do not invent standings that were not shown.
Do not use books, notes, calculators, computational aids, drawing aids, laptops, PDAs, phones, hidden solutions, or outside problem-solving help.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate discoveries needed by teammates. Later Guts sets are not shared team state until released.

competition_format: Official: Guts is an 80-minute team event with 36 short-answer questions on mixed subjects, of varying difficulty and printed point weights.
Official: problems are divided into sets of 3 in November or 4 in February.
Official: all teams gather in large lecture halls; at the starting signal a runner collects the first set for each teammate from an assigned problem station.
Official: this session is the Guts Round only; Individual tests and the Team Round are separate events.
Simulation choice: the runner loads one Guts packet for the selected season rather than a live multi-hall tournament.
timeline: Official: the Guts Round lasts 80 minutes.
Official: it is not expected that students will finish all the problems.
Official: as soon as a team has answers for one problem set, the runner may bring those answers to the problem station and pick up the next set.
Simulation choice: max_turns is a safety budget approximating the official clock, not a second official time limit.
Simulation choice: later sets remain unreleased until a current-set hand-in is specified by the task; the runner logistics are not executed as a physical state machine.
resource_policy: Official: books, notes, calculators, pocket organizers, slide-rules, abaci, and other computational aids are forbidden.
Official: graph paper, rulers, protractors, compasses, architectural tools, and other drawing aids are forbidden.
Official: laptops, PDAs, cell phones, and other communication devices are prohibited.
Official: paper and organizer-provided scratch paper are allowed.
Simulation choice: the only machine tool exposed is query_rules; do not claim a calculator, code runner, or public internet.
collaboration_protocol: Official: Guts is a team event; all members of the selected-season roster work together on the current set.
Official: November teams are 4–6 students and February teams are 6–8 students; eligibility is high-school students around the world.
Official: problem-solving communication is limited to teammates; coaches and other teams may not solve for you.
Simulation choice: every contestant starts with equal permissions; runner, scribe, or checker jobs may rotate and are never exclusive offices.
Simulation choice: private notes are unknown to teammates until communicated.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: computational aids, drawing aids, and communication devices are contest violations.
Official: outside problem-solving help is forbidden.
Official: written appeals go to the designated Appeals Room by the contest-day deadline; HMMT coordinators' decisions are final.
Simulation choice: do not access hidden answer keys, evaluator internals, or unreleased later sets.
Simulation choice: inventing teammates beyond the selected-season roster is a compliance violation.
deliverable_format: Official: Guts answers are short-answer single values.
Official: acceptable-answer conventions are those published with Testing Information.
Official: the runner submits the current set's answers at the problem station before receiving the next set.
Simulation choice: the runner accepts one shared numbered answer sheet of exact values when required.
Simulation choice: any contestant may file that shared sheet.
evaluation_criteria: Official: each Guts problem carries a point weight indicated on the exam; the raw Guts score is the sum of those weights for correct answers.
Official: grading is immediate and scores are posted in real time.
Official: Sweepstakes scales the top raw Guts score to 400 points and adds scaled Individual 800 and Team 400; that aggregate is not this session's score.
Simulation choice: repository evaluation is gold matching per problem_or_question and is deferred_benchmark_metadata_missing; do not invent a completed official grade.
Simulation choice: report Guts correctness separately from rule compliance and collaboration quality.
runtime_limitations: Official: progressive set release, runner pickup, irreversible hand-in, immediate grading, and a live scoreboard are contest-day facts.
Simulation choice: progressive_batch_release and batch_finality are specified only; the session does not unlock later sets or lock handed-in answers.
Official: the live scoreboard posts Guts scores during the round.
Simulation choice: no multi-team board is published to agents.
Simulation choice: limited team messaging is a benchmark overlay, not an official HMMT cap.
Simulation choice: season is a required selector on each benchmark row.
official_eligibility_and_season: Official: both tournaments are for high-school students around the world.
Official: November Guts uses sets of 3 and teams of 4–6; February Guts uses sets of 4 and teams of 6–8.
Simulation choice: November rows instantiate 6 contestants and February rows instantiate 8; smaller official November rosters of 4 or 5 are not instantiated.
Simulation choice: eligibility and on-site lecture-hall logistics are carried as contestant conscience, not as visa or attendance state machines.
appeals: Official: a student who believes an answer-key entry is incorrect must go to the designated Appeals Room and submit an appeal in writing.
Official: the appeal deadline is announced on the day of the contest.
Official: decisions of the HMMT coordinators are final.
Simulation choice: the Appeals Room is specified and not executed.

simulation.turn_budget_basis: official clock 16 turns vs floor 21 (8 teammates x 2 turns + 1 answer parts + 4 for synthesis)
